title: Choose the annotator's layout
question: Three layouts for the redesigned annotator, all in PartLabeler's own theme (your account's light/dark and accent still apply). The roll leads with the editor dock. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: Editor dock
options.lineage: video editing suites, V7's per-label timeline segments
options.thesis: The annotator as a video editor: the frame on top, every part a lane in the timeline below.
options.viewport: Slim header; canvas fills the top with a vertical tool rail (AI, Manual, View); below, a dock: transport row, then one lane per part showing where it is drawn, tracked or flagged, with classes beside it.
options.risk: Many parts make many lanes: learners can drown unless lanes collapse to the selected part.

options.label: Rail and inspector
options.lineage: CVAT, Label Studio, V7 annotation workviews
options.thesis: The map annotators already know, rebuilt properly: tools left, inspector right, frames below.
options.viewport: Left tool rail grouped AI / Manual / View with a contextual options bar above the frame; right inspector with tabs Classes, Parts, Find, Export; bottom transport with Confirm and Delete frame over the status ribbon.
options.risk: Familiar to the point of anonymity: its character has to come from the ribbon and the finish.

options.label: Label and Review modes
options.lineage: CVAT's workspace switcher, darkroom contact sheets
options.thesis: Two workspaces behind one switch: draw in Label, judge in Review, so nobody faces everything at once.
options.viewport: Header with a Label | Review switch. Label: tool rail, class list, canvas. Review: canvas over a large filmstrip where flagged frames rise, with big Confirm and Delete frame.
options.risk: A mode switch costs a keystroke, and experts may resent tools hidden while reviewing.
